law: A licence is a MEASUREMENT and measurements drift. This file is the floor each measured mapping must keep clearing; the scoreboard counter compares the live licence file against it every run. Before this existed nothing asserted NFL.com agreement at all -- if def_pass_defended regressed from 97.7% to 40%, no test and no counter would have moved. A floor is not a target: the two MAPPING-SUSPECT rows are recorded at their MEASURED value so that a further slide is caught even though they are not licensed.
why_a_counter_and_not_a_test: A test that needs an off-repo artifact pytest.skips without it, so it is not a gate. The counter runs every time and reports a floor with NO licence row as a violation rather than as a pass.
stratum: 2005-2019, validate()'s known-good modern stratum. Verdicts outside it are NOT covered by these floors: on this table pdef reads 99.1% on 2010+ and 0.0% before 1982, so a single blended floor would be meaningless.
tolerance: EXACT (stat_contracts tolerance_policy, EXACT_EPS 1e-6). The +/-1.5 band this lane used until 2026-07-31 licensed def_safeties at ~100% while it contradicted us on 143 of 143 rows in 1982-93.
publication_filter: TRY_CAST, not IS NOT NULL -- NFL.com writes '' where a column does not apply, and an unpublished row scored as a disagreement until 2026-07-31.
licence_key_note: FLOORS ARE ONE PER (source, v26_col) BECAUSE THAT IS THE LICENCE KEY, and on nflcom_player_career that key is NOT UNIQUE: QB / RBFB / WRTE Career all map onto fumbles, fumbles_lost, carries, rushing_yards and rushing_tds, and RBFB/WRTE also share the four receiving canonicals -- 9 colliding keys in all. MapSpec was given a source_table for exactly this reason; the licence key never was. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and the first reading was wrong: 5 of the 9 return an identical agree_pct but 4 DIFFER -- fumbles .9071/.9073/.9082, fumbles_lost .9541/.9543/.9551, receiving_long .9955/.9957 -- because each position page carries a slightly different player population, so the collision is not benign even though the spread is <= 0.0011. The floor therefore takes the MINIMUM across the colliding tables, so the gate cannot be tripped by which table happened to be written, and source_table records every table the floor was measured on.

equation_floor_law: The equation lane produced receipts and nothing compared against them, so a rate measured at 0.9899 could have gone to 0.5 with no gate moving -- the same 'measurement nobody watches' state the licence floors exist to end, rebuilt one layer over. These are keyed by DOSSIER ROW rather than by (source, v26_col), because a rate is checked by an EXPRESSION and not by a licensed mapping, and a declared floor with no measurement counts as a violation exactly as a missing licence does.
week_grain_floor_law: TRIMMED 2026-07-31: the 54 counting columns now have real week-grain MapSpecs (shape='nflcom_week' against the recovered table) and are watched by LICENCE floors like anything else. What remains here is the 11 rate/formula arms, which are checked by an EXPRESSION and correctly have no value path.
aggregate_floor_law: g/gs are a coarser-grain value checked against a SEASON-table canonical, so they are neither a licensed mapping nor a two-operand ratio and fall through both other floor kinds. They are watched at their MEASURED value (0.6295 / 0.6038), NOT at a quality bar: a floor is a REGRESSION guard, and a mapping already known to disagree must still not silently disagree MORE. The disagreement itself is filed as a SUPERTABLE_VALUE defect -- three-way nflcom~PFR 98.9-99.3%, both against us 51.6-77.1%, one-sided 30,296 to 167 -- and repairing it will RAISE this floor, which is the point.
population_scoped_floor_law: SCOPING IS A DECISION, NOT A FILTER -- narrowing a comparison until it agrees is how an audit lies to itself. Each floor carries BOTH numbers so the move is always visible, and the population declares why the source is scoped plus the control proving scope is the cause (92.9% of the 1,448 disputed player-games are offensive linemen, against a population where G+OT are ~1,500 of 119,000 tackle-bearing weeks). APPLIED TO tkl (.7653 -> .8980) AND combined (.7586 -> .8920) ONLY. `ast` was measured the same way and got WORSE (.9570 -> .9505), so it is NOT scoped -- offensive linemen tackling after a turnover make SOLO tackles, so removing them helps solo/combined and does nothing for assists. A population that improved every column it touched would be a knob, not a finding.
staleness_law: EVERY OTHER CHECK IN THIS CONTRACT COMPARES A FLOOR AGAINST A MEASUREMENT LEDGER, which catches a value that MOVED and is blind to a ledger that was never RE-RUN. If the v26 release changes and nobody re-measures, every floor still passes and the gate reads green -- the green-means-captured failure this programme has already paid for, rebuilt one layer over. So the floors pin the release they were measured against and a mismatch is itself a violation: the gate FAILS until the audit is re-run, rather than silently comparing new data to an old floor. Absence of the field is also a violation, because 'I cannot tell whether I am stale' is not a pass.
ratchet_law: A FLOOR MAY RISE FREELY AND MAY NEVER SILENTLY FALL. Every other check here compares a MEASUREMENT against a FLOOR, which is defeated completely by editing the floor -- proven 2026-07-31 by lowering one to 0.01, after which the gate read GREEN with no record. `high_water` is the best value a floor has ever held; dropping below it requires a reasoned entry in `ratchet_exemptions`, so weakening the standard leaves a trace instead of being invisible. A floor with NO high_water is itself a violation, because an un-ratcheted floor is one edit from meaningless. Repairing a defect RAISES the high_water, which is the direction this is meant to move.
conservation_law: PLAYERS MUST AGGREGATE TO TEAMS AND MUST MATCH THEMSELVES. The column audit asks neither: its subject is one player's one column, and the team-DEF plane carries no pfr_id so it never reaches the crosswalk every nflcom measurement runs through -- 19% to 81% of the defensive material was invisible to '200 columns gated'. SPLIT, and the split is the finding: def_fumbles_forced (.9972-1.0000), def_interceptions (.9544-.9991), def_pass_defended (.9930) and def_tackle_assists (.9643) HOLD; def_sacks holds modern (.9652-.9829) and fails pre-1994 (.5413); def_safeties fails everywhere (.0201-.6468, IDP always SHORT and ONE-SIDED); def_tackles_solo and def_tackles_combined fail at .1725/.1692 with IDP OVER. INTERNAL consistency is near-perfect on both planes -- combined = solo + assists holds .9990-1.0000 on idp_rows every era and 1.0000 on team_def_row -- so each plane is self-coherent and they disagree with EACH OTHER. A HYPOTHESIS THAT DIED HERE, so it is not retried: the tackles_solo overshoot looked like the offensive-lineman tail found the same day. Restricting the IDP side to DB/LB/DL makes it WORSE (.1725 -> .1130) and the tail is 7,682 tackles at a median of 1 per team-week. The team row matches neither population.
subject_level_floors_law: season == SUM/MAX(weekly) and career == SUM/MAX(season), per column, with the aggregate chosen by the DECLARED aggregation_class. Seeded 2026-07-31 from subject_level_recon.py. ONLY checks already at or above 0.995 are floored -- flooring a failing check at its failing value is how a ratchet cements a defect (punt_long would have been locked at 0.9781 forever). The 34 below the bar are QUEUED with their reason, not floored. This is an INTERNAL consistency check, not a witness: all planes can be identically wrong, so it never votes -- but a disagreement is unambiguously ours.

season_plane_equation_floors_law: A PUBLISHED RATE IS A WITNESS ON WHATEVER PLANE ITS OPERANDS ARE READ FROM. Until 2026-07-31 audit_capacity_runner always read sources.latest_v26() -- the WEEKLY release -- so every rate verified our weekly->season ROLLUP and never the STORED season table. Joe raised this three times ('avg is just another way to witness on the season and career levels'); it was recorded twice and built the third time. It matters because the stored plane is exactly where kickoff_return_long / punt_long / punt_return_long were being SUMMED instead of maxed with nothing watching. These 10 floors watch the stored plane. Eight give agreement identical to the weekly rollup; the two KICKING rates do not -- K Career pct 0.9274 -> 0.9276 and xpct 0.8900 -> 0.8903 -- and the row counts are the tell (2,095 -> 2,098 and 2,110 -> 2,114), because the stored plane carries player-seasons the weekly rollup cannot produce. CAREER grain is NOT covered here: the nflcom career pages publish per-SEASON rows and no career-total row, so there is no external career rate to compare against -- a career check would be internal, not a witness. SEEDED FROM THE LANE'S LEDGER, NOT FROM A HAND MEASUREMENT. The first seeding used my own ad-hoc run_one() calls and P Career avg came out 0.9661 where the lane measures 0.9657 -- the lane applies the row_filter from each column's audit_capacity declaration and my call did not. A floor seeded above what the lane can reproduce fails the gate forever, which is how it was caught.
